doc.title: Ralph LaLama interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, May 23, 2010

title: Woody Herman tag in 'Like Someone in Love' and teaching freedom beyond the Real Book
summary: A lick he played came from Woody's band; he tells students the Real Book is only a guide.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: And speaking of learning, I have this thing that came to me yesterday when you were playing, and it has something to do with teaching I think, because I mean you can learn the Real Book tunes and all that, but there was stuff that you guys did yesterday that I was wondering where it came from. And one of example was you did the tune “Like Someone In Love.” And near the end of it, right at the end, you played a lick, it was sort of a tag, and it sounded like: “My mama done told me.”
Exactly right. That’s my Woody influence.
So where does that come from and how do you, as a teacher, get your kids to learn all that?

That’s my experience. That’s where that came from. I didn’t think about it. We used to play it in Woody’s band: “My mama done told me/to bring home the” you know whatever the words. You know, “Blues in the Night.” And then when you live the stuff, see that’s what I mean, when you live the stuff, see that’s what I mean, when you learn it in the Real Book sometimes you’re not living it unless you play it for a couple of years, you know, a song let’s say. And that’s all. And that came to my mind, because that was part of my musical growing up, you know?
Okay. So that thing wasn’t an outtro so to speak that I should have known about?
Okay, you just — it sounded just like it was part of it.
But it fit. I try to be melodic, musical. Yeah, that’s right. Yeah, you’ve got to make all this fit. And that’s through experience you know?
Yeah, but there was a couple of other things too, like some intros and stuff that you don’t see in the Real Book.
I guess that as a teacher you may pass those on to your students.

I might show them different ways they can go with things. The reason why I would do that, not that they would copy me, they maybe copy me for a little bit but mainly so that they realize they have the freedom to do that, to use their own ingenuity, their own creativeness. You don’t have to just read it like a book. You know there’s a lot of people

when they learn from the Real Books and stuff, they think oh we have to do it like the book. But the book says that. No it’s not. I mean that’s not The Bible. All it is is a guide. That’s the same way you play chord changes. You know because it says this doesn’t mean you can’t use that, you know, but it has to sound right. That’s what I mean. That’s where taste comes in. You know? And tension and all. Ahhh.
You know what, you can use that when you go back and teach.
Well I do, I think I do. But I’ll even use it more because it makes more sense now.
